title: Identify the actual coefficient quotient-cone comparison with completion exchange
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and finite coefficient fields inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation rings, uniformizers and finite quotients as in [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. For a field $F$ write $R_F=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,s}=\lim_n B_{F,n}$ and $B_{F,n}=(\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^n)_s$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves on the small pro-etale site of $s$, with the coefficient universes of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. Put $H_F=\mathcal L_s^F\mathcal R_s^F$, with actual unit $u^F$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], normalized by [lem-trf-completion-unit-strict-quotient-model]. On the full derived-complete subcategory [def-weil-derived-complete] write $v^F=(u^F)^{-1}$, using [lem-pur-normalized-reconstruction-adjunction-calculus].

Let $E\subset L$, set $R=R_E$, $S=R_L$, $t=\varpi_E$, $w=\varpi_L$, and $T=-\otimes_R^L S$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $\widehat T$ for the specified strict-tower integral scalar extension [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined] and $\chi: T\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat T$ on complete objects for [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Let $C\in D(R)$ be derived complete. For a flat-term K-flat representative $P\to C$, use the normalized Roos cones [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

The projection $R_F\to B_{F,n}$ identifies $R_F/\varpi_F^nR_F$ with $B_{F,n}$, compatibly with all quotient transitions, for $F=E,L$. Under these identifications the strict sheaf-quotient completions of [lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange] are naturally $H_E,H_L$, and their augmentations are the actual $u^E,u^L$. The multiplication identification
$$ (P\otimes_R S)\otimes_S B_{L,n}\longrightarrow P\otimes_R B_{L,n},\quad (p\otimes a)\otimes b\longmapsto p\otimes ab $$
identifies $\widehat TC$ with $H_L(TC)$ in $D(S)$ and carries $\chi_C$ to $u^L_{TC}$; this is natural in complete $C$, including $C$ replaced by $H_EC$.

Define $b_C:T(H_EC)\to H_L(TC)$ by the canonical tensor/product comparison and the map on both Roos product coordinates induced at index $n$ by
$$ (p\otimes\bar a)\otimes z\longmapsto p\otimes\iota_n(\bar a)\bar z, $$
where $\iota_n:\mathcal O_E/t^n\to\mathcal O_L/w^n$ is the quotient map of [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-well-defined]. This specifies a natural derived map independent of representatives. For complete $C$ it equals the exchange $\epsilon_C$ of [lem-pur-finite-free-completion-exchange], after the preceding quotient identifications; thus this assertion compares the same-index quotient map with the arithmetic-subsequence exchange, rather than choosing a comparison by an equation. The specified completed comparison
$$ \beta_{L/E,C}=H_L(\chi_C)\,b_C\,\chi_{H_EC}^{-1}:\widehat T(H_EC)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_L(\widehat TC) $$
satisfies the equality of actual derived morphisms
$$ v^L_{\widehat TC}\,\beta_{L/E,C}=\widehat T(v^E_C). $$
This holds for ramified extensions as well, with no boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor assumption on $C$.

source.place: First sentence, 'for f=id_s the functor Rf_! is the identity': the coefficient-sheaf quotient and tower identifications, equality of the same-index scalar comparison with completion exchange on complete inputs, and completed conjugation (old steps 5-7).

external.place: Definitions 3.5.2-3.5.3, Lemma 3.5.7 and Lemma 6.8.2(1). Agent-formulated comparison and descent calculation extracted from the returned proof, not a verbatim theorem of this source.

proof.text: The completed_exact theorem supplies invertibility of both actual quotient comparisons. Cancel their cokernel projections to prove adjacent transition compatibility, then apply the single-complex functor. This is the private quotientTransitions proof.

Use the existing counit-normalized completed scalar cochain model; its ordinary and derived functors give hE and sigma by reflexivity. Finite freeness and the ramification relation from the completed scalar comparison proof instantiate finiteFreeQuotientRoosComparison. Apply the existing exchangeFromCochains construction to obtain CR, CS, epsilon and their entire unit equation, retaining the prescribed arithmetic representative formulas.

Apply the normalized quotient-adjunction realization to CR and CS, and multiplication realization to F and CS. These supply A,B,ME,ML,NE,NL,alpha,gamma,c and the complete normalization equations required in the statement. Apply same-index descent to F,CR,CS to obtain b with its representative formula and entire unit equation.

For complete K, normalized reconstruction gives completeness of H_E K and invertibility of its actual unit. Finite-free scalar comparison gives completeness of T K and invertibility of chi at K and H_E K. Naturality of the target unit along chi_K makes the target unit at widehat T K invertible. The normalized quotient-unit criterion transfers this to actual completeness. Apply the same criterion to CR at K; cancel F.T.map(CR.unit_K) in the two whole-unit equations to prove b_K=epsilon_K.

Transport the b unit equation along alpha, gamma and sigma; their naturality and inverse equations give T(actual source unit) followed by actualSameIndex equals the actual target unit. Set beta=widehat T(uK inverse) followed by uX. After left composition with chi_H, naturality of chi at uK inverse and of the target unit at chi_K proves exactly the requested conjugation expression. Right composition with uX inverse then cancels uX and proves the final derived-morphism identity. The private sameIndex_actual_unit and conjugated_unit proofs carry out these cancellations explicitly.

proof_origin.place: Opening sentence, coefficient normalization; implements the existing nine-step comparison argument using three strictly smaller construction/descent lemmas and explicit categorical cancellation.
